vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agentic-commerce-forthecult
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle is designed for a legitimate e-commerce purpose, enabling an AI agent to browse products, place orders, and track shipments on `https://forthecult.store/api`. All API interactions are confined to this single domain. Crucially, the `SKILL.md` contains multiple, explicit guardrails instructing the AI agent *not* to follow URLs or endpoint paths from API responses (`error.suggestions`, `_actions`) that point to any other host or to undocumented paths. While `references/ERRORS.md` contains a slightly ambiguous phrase about following suggested endpoints, the overwhelming context, examples, and repeated warnings in `SKILL.md` clearly restrict the agent to the documented API. There is no evidence of intentional malicious behavior such as data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, backdoors, or arbitrary code execution.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only integration that coherently documents a REST API for browsing, ordering, and tracking purchases (including optional on-chain wallet-based discounts); it requests no credentials or installs and its runtime instructions match the stated purpose, though there are a few minor notes about privacy and behavior to be aware of.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (agentic shopping, multi-chain payments, order tracking) aligns with the documented endpoints (search, product details, /checkout, /orders/{id}/status, /chains). No unrelated credentials, binaries, or installs are requested. Minor mismatch: SKILL.md says “No API key or authentication needed” while the API reference documents an optional GET /api/agent/me endpoint that requires an X-Moltbook-Identity header (reasonable for agent identity, but worth noting).

dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: All instructions are limited to calling the store API at https://forthecult.store (search, product detail, checkout, status). The skill explicitly requires collecting user-supplied data needed for purchases (email, shipping address, and optionally walletAddress for discounts). It also directs agents to auto-follow API-provided `error.suggestions` and to poll order status frequently (e.g., every 5s while awaiting payment). These behaviors are coherent for autonomous checkout but raise operational/privacy considerations (see guidance).

llm.guidance: This skill is internally consistent and appears to be what it claims: an agent-facing wrapper around https://forthecult.store for browsing and placing orders (including crypto payments). Before installing or enabling it, consider: (1) Privacy — the agent will ask for email, full shipping address, and may request a blockchain wallet address to compute CULT discounts; only provide the wallet address if you understand that it links on-chain holdings to your order. (2) Payments — the checkout flow returns a crypto address and amount; ensure agents always require explicit user confirmation before sending or instructing payment, and verify the payment address/amount shown to you. (3) Auto-retries and suggestions — the skill recommends automatically following API `suggestions` and polling frequently; configure limits to avoid excessive calls or unintended actions. (4) Identity header — some agent-specific endpoints mention an X-Moltbook-Identity header (agent runtime identity); confirm your agent runtime supplies appropriate identity headers if you expect to call those endpoints. (5) Verify the domain and support contact (weare@forthecult.store) if you have concerns about legitimacy. If you want stricter safety, require manual approval before any checkout or payment step and do not auto-send wallet addresses.
